title: अध्याय ६४

items.speaker: ; मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
एवं विमुक्तरोगा तु कन्यका तं मुदान्विता ।
स्वरोचिषमुवाचेदं शृणुष्व वचनं प्रभो ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ vimuktarogā tu kanyakā taṃ mudānvitā |
svarociṣamuvācedaṃ śṛṇuṣva vacanaṃ prabho || 1 ||

items.text:
मन्दारविद्याधरजा नाम्ना ख्याता विभावरी ।
उपकारिन् ! स्वमात्मानं प्रयच्छामि प्रतीच्छ माम् ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
mandāravidyādharajā nāmnā khyātā vibhāvarī |
upakārin ! svamātmānaṃ prayacchāmi pratīccha mām || 2 ||

items.text:
विद्याञ्च तुभ्यं दास्यामि सर्वबूतरुतानि ते ।
ययाभिव्यक्तिमेष्यन्ति प्रसादपुरगो भव ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
vidyāñca tubhyaṃ dāsyāmi sarvabūtarutāni te |
yayābhivyaktimeṣyanti prasādapurago bhava || 3 ||

items.speaker: ; मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
एवमस्त्विति तेनोक्ते धर्मज्ञेन स्वरोचिषा ।
द्वितीया तु तदा कन्या इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
evamastviti tenokte dharmajñena svarociṣā |
dvitīyā tu tadā kanyā idaṃ vacanamabravīt || 4 ||

items.text:
कुमारब्रह्मचार्यासीत् पारो नाम पिता मम ।
ब्रह्मर्षिः सुमहाभागो वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
kumārabrahmacāryāsīt pāro nāma pitā mama |
brahmarṣiḥ sumahābhāgo vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ || 5 ||

items.text:
तस्य पुंस्कोकिलालापरमणीये मधौ पुरा ।
आजगामाप्सराभ्यासं प्रख्याता पुञ्जिकास्तना ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
tasya puṃskokilālāparamaṇīye madhau purā |
ājagāmāpsarābhyāsaṃ prakhyātā puñjikāstanā || 6 ||

items.text:
कामवक्तव्यतां नीतः स तदा मुनिपुङ्गवः ।
तत्संयोगेऽहमुत्पन्ना तस्यामत्र महाचले ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
kāmavaktavyatāṃ nītaḥ sa tadā munipuṅgavaḥ |
tatsaṃyoge'hamutpannā tasyāmatra mahācale || 7 ||

items.text:
विहाय मां गता सा च मातास्मिन्निर्जने वने ।
बालामेकां महीपृष्ठे व्यालश्वापदसंकुले ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
vihāya māṃ gatā sā ca mātāsminnirjane vane |
bālāmekāṃ mahīpṛṣṭhe vyālaśvāpadasaṃkule || 8 ||

items.text:
ततः कलाभिः सोमस्य वर्धन्तीभिरहः क्षये ।
आप्याय्यमानाहरहो वृद्धिं यातास्मि सत्तम ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ kalābhiḥ somasya vardhantībhirahaḥ kṣaye |
āpyāyyamānāharaho vṛddhiṃ yātāsmi sattama || 9 ||

items.text:
ततः कलावतीत्येतन्मम नाम महात्मना ।
गृहीतायः कृतं पित्रा गन्धर्वेण शुभानना ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ kalāvatītyetanmama nāma mahātmanā |
gṛhītāyaḥ kṛtaṃ pitrā gandharveṇa śubhānanā || 10 ||

items.text:
न दत्ताहं तदा तेन याचितेन महात्मना ।
देवारिणालिना सुप्तस्ततो मे घातितः पिता ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
na dattāhaṃ tadā tena yācitena mahātmanā |
devāriṇālinā suptastato me ghātitaḥ pitā || 11 ||

items.text:
मा शुचः सुभ्रु ! भर्ता ते महाभागो भविष्यति ।
स्वरोचिर्नाम पुत्रश्च मनुस्तस्य भविष्यति ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
mā śucaḥ subhru ! bhartā te mahābhāgo bhaviṣyati |
svarocirnāma putraśca manustasya bhaviṣyati || 13 ||

items.text:
आज्ञाञ्च निधयः सर्वे करिष्यन्ति तवादृताः ।
यथाभिलषितं वित्तं प्रदास्यन्ति च ते शुभे ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
ājñāñca nidhayaḥ sarve kariṣyanti tavādṛtāḥ |
yathābhilaṣitaṃ vittaṃ pradāsyanti ca te śubhe || 14 ||

items.text:
यस्या वत्से प्रभावेण विद्यायास्तां गृहाण मे ।
पद्मिनी नाम विद्येयं महापद्माभिपूजिता ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
yasyā vatse prabhāveṇa vidyāyāstāṃ gṛhāṇa me |
padminī nāma vidyeyaṃ mahāpadmābhipūjitā || 15 ||

items.text:
इत्याह मां दक्षसुता सती सत्यपरायणा ।
स्वरोचिस्त्वं ध्रुवं देवी नान्यथा सा वदिष्यति ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
ityāha māṃ dakṣasutā satī satyaparāyaṇā |
svarocistvaṃ dhruvaṃ devī nānyathā sā vadiṣyati || 16 ||

items.text:
साहं प्राणप्रदायाद्य तां विद्यां स्वं तथा वपुः ।
प्रयच्छामि प्रतीच्छ त्वं प्रसादसुमुखो मम ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
sāhaṃ prāṇapradāyādya tāṃ vidyāṃ svaṃ tathā vapuḥ |
prayacchāmi pratīccha tvaṃ prasādasumukho mama || 17 ||

items.speaker: ; मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
एवमस्त्विति तामाह स तु कन्यां कलावतीम् ।
विभावर्याः कलावत्याः स्निग्धदृष्ट्यानुमोदितः ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
evamastviti tāmāha sa tu kanyāṃ kalāvatīm |
vibhāvaryāḥ kalāvatyāḥ snigdhadṛṣṭyānumoditaḥ || 18 ||

items.text:
जग्राह च ततः पाणी स तयोरमरद्युतिः ।
नदत्सु देवतूर्येषु नृत्यन्तीष्वप्सरः सु च ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
jagrāha ca tataḥ pāṇī sa tayoramaradyutiḥ |
nadatsu devatūryeṣu nṛtyantīṣvapsaraḥ su ca || 19 ||

en_summary: Markandeya continues telling Kraushtuki the story of Svarochis. The girl whom Svarochis has just freed from her illness speaks to him with joy: she is Vibhavari, daughter of Mandara the vidyadhara; she offers herself to him in return for his help and promises him a skill (vidya) by which he will understand the cries of all living beings. Svarochis, who knows dharma, agrees. Then the second girl speaks. Her father was Para, a great Brahmin sage who lived as a celibate from youth and had mastered the Vedas and their branches. Once in spring, when the cuckoos were calling, the famous apsaras Punjikastana came near him; he was overcome by desire, and from their union she was born on this great mountain. Her mother left her alone as a baby on the ground in the empty forest full of snakes and wild beasts, and she grew day by day, nourished by the growing phases (kalas) of the moon; so her father, a great gandharva who took her in, named her Kalavati. When a demon, an enemy of the gods, asked for her and her father refused, the demon killed him while he slept. In deep despair she was about to kill herself, but Sati, the truthful wife of Shiva and daughter of Daksha, stopped her: she said Kalavati would have a great husband named Svarochis, his son would be a Manu, and all the treasures (nidhis) would obey her and give her whatever wealth she wanted through the skill called Padmini, honoured by the treasure Mahapadma, which Sati gave her. Since Sati never speaks falsely, Kalavati says, he must be Svarochis, and she gives him this skill and herself, since he has saved her life. With Vibhavari's loving approval he accepts Kalavati too, and the godlike Svarochis takes the hands of both girls in marriage while divine drums sound and apsaras dance.
